idiom_name: FnMut closures over the locals; local struct with impl and &mut self as the escalation
implementation_notes: Closures capture their environment by shared reference, mutable reference or move (Rust reference), which is exactly the method object's shared state: a closure that mutates a captured local implements FnMut, and a step consumed once may implement FnOnce. The limit is the borrow checker - two closures that both need &mut to the same accumulator cannot coexist, and the working answer is to promote the group to a struct with impl methods taking &mut self, declared locally inside the function when it must stay private. Choose the struct form when the state must be named, tested or shared by several mutating steps; keep closures for one or two steps.
pitfalls: Two closures that mutate the same local both borrow it mutably and the borrow checker rejects the pair; a struct with &mut self methods is the clean fix, while RefCell moves the check to runtime and loses the compile-time guarantee.
A closure capturing by reference cannot outlive the enclosing function, so returning it or spawning it needs move - and then the state is owned by the closure instead of shared with the caller.
Before Rust 2021 a closure captured whole variables rather than individual fields, which can borrow more of a struct than the step actually needs.
